page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 62.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, which includes 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and relies on external storage options, while network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance scales to average levels, matching the middle 50% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register average throughput, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%. The standout capability of this instance lies in its GPU-accelerated workloads; LLM inference prompt processing for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models achieves top-tier performance in the top 10%, while text generation for the 7B model is rated as strong in the top 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU makes this instance a viable entry point for GPU-accelerated tasks without the higher overhead of larger accelerator classes. The tradeoff is the lower single-core CPU performance and lack of local storage, which requires careful architecture around network-attached storage. This server is highly suited for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, video transcoding, and general-purpose GPU computing where massive CPU single-thread performance is not the primary bottleneck.
